Deviation

/dee-vee-AY-shun/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Deviation means a departure from an established course, standard, or norm.

Deviation means a departure from an established course, standard, or norm. Air traffic controllers noticed a small deviation from the flight plan and radioed the pilot to ask why the jet had drifted south of its approved route.

Worked Example

The bakery's famous sourdough had been made the same way for forty years, so when Wednesday's loaves came out darker and tangier than usual, the head baker traced the deviation to a new apprentice who had let the dough rise an extra hour.

The change in the loaves is a departure from the bakery's long-established standard recipe, which is exactly what a deviation is.

How Deviation Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

departure

departure: a turning away from a usual course

divergence

divergence: a moving apart from a set path

irregularity

irregularity: something that does not follow the usual rule

Antonyms

conformity

conformity: behavior that follows the accepted standard

adherence

adherence: faithful sticking to a rule or path

How Strong Is It? — variation → deviation → defiance

variation vs. deviation

variation vs. deviation: A variation is a mild, often expected difference within the normal range, while a deviation is a clear departure from the established course or standard.

defiance vs. deviation

defiance vs. deviation: A deviation steps away from the norm, but defiance openly rejects the rule itself.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of deviation.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — de-

Prefix — de-: off, away from

Root — via

Root — via: from Latin via, road, way

Suffix — -tion

Suffix — -tion: noun-forming ending, act or result of

Put it together

Put it together: Deviation is built from de-, 'off, away from,' the Latin root via, 'road or way,' and the noun ending -tion. A deviation is literally a step 'off the road,' a departure from the path or standard that everyone expected to be followed.

Use the root in a new word: obvious

Use the root in a new word: obvious: The answer was obvious to everyone in the room, and the word itself began as Latin obvius, 'lying in the way, right there on the road,' the same via root found in deviation.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral, often technical

Deviation names the act or an instance of departing from a course, standard, or norm, and it is the noun relative of the verb deviate, also taught in this unit. It is common in technical phrases such as 'standard deviation' in statistics and 'deviation from protocol' in formal reports.
